name: La salle d'attente
camera: standing by the south window, facing north into the waiting room (front door on the east = right)

setting.walls: sage-green wooden wainscot to waist height, pale warm-grey plaster above with a few framed botanical prints (no text)
setting.floor: honey oak herringbone parquet with a round woven rug
setting.landmark: a big round aquarium on a carved wooden stand in the middle of the back wall, with a tall rubber plant beside it
setting.light: soft daylight from the glazed front door and a tall window on the left
setting.style: S07 gentle storybook painterly 3.5/5 (one style for the whole Quartier de la Santé)

items.scene: A rosy, fit grandma standing in a bright SUN-beam raises her cup of TEA ("sahn-TAY") to wish everyone good HEALTH.
A FAT TIGER cub ("fah-TEEG") lies sprawled asleep across two waiting-room chairs, worn out with TIREDNESS, one paw dangling.
A penguin with the FLU, scarf round its neck, GRIPS ("GREEP") a hot-water bottle tight and sneezes a puff of snowflakes.
A girl with a COUGH covers her face politely, and the TOUCAN ("TOO") perched on her chair back looks on with concern.
A puppy leaps up at the little coat-cupboard DOOR ("DUHR") with such ARDOUR that its tail is a blur.
A grumpy green fuzzy VIRUS ("vee-REWS") puppet bounces off old RUTH's open umbrella as she sits waiting.

Sue (recurring character: a cheerful 10-year-old girl with two black bunches tied with yellow ribbons, red raincoat, yellow wellies) lifts a huge sack of potatoes off a LARGE MAN's back ("soo-LAHZH-MAHN"), and he sighs with RELIEF, arms flung wide.

prompt:
Gentle storybook painterly illustration, realism about 3.5/5, soft gouache-and-oil brushwork, warm-hearted and calm, natural NEUTRAL daylight with true colours, off-white whites, no orange, sepia, amber or golden cast, no pink or blue tint, clear readable figures with contact shadows on the floor, consistent eye-level perspective, 16:9 wide composition.
Scene: La salle d'attente in the B17_cabinet building, ground floor (front, south). Camera: standing by the south window, facing north into the waiting room (front door on the east = right).
Setting: sage-green wooden wainscot to waist height, pale warm-grey plaster above with a few framed botanical prints (no text); floor: honey oak herringbone parquet with a round woven rug. Landmark: a big round aquarium on a carved wooden stand in the middle of the back wall, with a tall rubber plant beside it. Light: soft daylight from the glazed front door and a tall window on the left. The room feels lived-in and real, with depth (never an empty white backdrop).
Paint these exits clearly as walkable openings: an open arch on the LEFT (west) wall showing a primrose-yellow room (way to Le cabinet ORL); a wooden staircase climbing UP at the BACK LEFT along the north wall (way to Le palier); a white panelled door at the BACK RIGHT (way to Le cabinet du docteur); the glazed green front door on the RIGHT (east) wall with the square's cobbles beyond (way to Dehors).
Characters and objects, each a separate, clearly spaced group, feminine-word groups on the left half and masculine-word groups on the right half:
- left, foreground: In a bright SUN-beam a rosy, fit grandma raises her cup of TEA to wish everyone good HEALTH.
- left, middle distance: A FAT TIGER cub lies sprawled asleep across two waiting-room chairs, worn out with TIREDNESS, one paw dangling.
- centre-left, foreground: A penguin with the FLU, scarf round its neck, GRIPS a hot-water bottle tight and sneezes a puff of snowflakes.
- centre, middle distance: A girl with a COUGH coughs politely into her elbow, and the TOUCAN on her shoulder covers its big beak with a wing too.
- centre-right, foreground: A puppy leaps up at the little coat-cupboard DOOR with such ARDOUR that its tail is a blur.
- right, middle distance: A grumpy green fuzzy VIRUS puppet bounces off old RUTH's open umbrella as she sits waiting.
- right, foreground: Sue, a cheerful 10-year-old girl with two black bunches tied with yellow ribbons, a red raincoat and yellow wellies, lifts a huge sack of potatoes off a LARGE MAN's back, and he sighs with RELIEF, arms flung wide.
Leave a blank light board for the room sign high on the back wall. No written words, letters, numbers or logos anywhere (signs and plaques are blank boards). No blood, no wounds, no needles in skin (syringes only as capped harmless props), no alcohol, no smoking, no religious symbols, no red-cross emblem. Nobody cropped by the image edge; keep every figure well inside the frame with a clear gap between figures. Figures stand on the floor or sit on real furniture, never floating or in rows behind a counter.
